newsitem.title: USA: Sen. Strom Thurmond released from hospital.
newsitem.headline: Sen. Strom Thurmond released from hospital.

text.p: Sen. Strom Thurmond, at 94 the oldest member of Congress, was released from a hospital Monday in time to preside over the opening of the Senate's daily session.

Thurmond's press secretary, Chris Cimka, said the South Carolina Republican was admitted to Walter Reed Medical Centre last week with the flu. He was advised to enter the hospital because of his age and because he lives alone, Cimka said.
"It's nothing more than the flu," she said. "You can't keep him down."

Thurmond is the president pro tem, or presiding officer, of the Senate, and prides himself on being present at the start of each day's session. He was re-elected last November for an eighth term that will keep him in office past his 100th birthday and has not ruled out running for a ninth term.
